seconds.summary: I read both files of Gauge III in full and attacked every statement: hypotheses, the mod-5 wrap-around, degenerate cases, z against -z, eta against eta^{-1}, the rings involved, the omitted arguments and every later use in the manuscript. All statements are true as written and all proofs are complete. I found no fatal error, no gap and no fixable error. I re-derived by hand the diagonal of the gauge (checked against symplecticity at z^0), the general symplectic form with r != r~ that cor:mai-univ uses, the vanishing-solution recursion against its closed form for n = 0..6, and r_1 = 3/5. I also checked the HPF identity with my own wolframscript script. There are five minor findings; two are new (F4, F5's second bullet). The other three confirm the first referee. F5 is a later remark (rmk:set-qrrsign) that cites lem:gau-HPF for more than the lemma proves; U01_C and L5 already reported it.

seconds.summary: Section 4 (transport) holds up: I found no fatal error, no gap and nothing that needs a repair. I re-derived every formula and sign, including the z/-z conventions, R against R^{-1}, the lowered and vector forms of (Sp) (they agree because eta^{-1}=eta/25), the mod-5 grading and the empty and n=0 cases. I also opened every cited statement and checked every later use in s05, s06, s07 and s10 against what the unit proves. Two independent exact-arithmetic scripts found no counterexample. escalations.title: eq:con-bz in Theorem P(a) proved factor by factor outside the ring it names
escalations.reason: eq:con-bz is true, and the factor-by-factor proof is valid once it is done in the right ring. The text names A_L(zeta)[[t]][[z]], which contains none of the factors. The right ring is B = A_L(zeta)[[t]]((z))[log z, log 5L, log(L-zeta^j)], with logarithms taken additively and T_z = exp(z d/dt) as a ring endomorphism of B. Two facts make it work. The Stirling series is consistent under a change of base point: T_z o eps = eps o tau_theta, two continuous ring homomorphisms that agree on generators. And lem:fsp-stirfe, iterated through tau_i tau_j = tau_{i+j}, gives each factor's shift. Choosing log q := -5 log 5L + sum_j log(L-zeta^j) makes all symbols cancel; exponentiating the remainder gives eq:con-bz in A_L[[t,z]]. U13-1/10, U14-2/3 and U14-5 are slips closed by lem:fsp-const or by renaming the intermediate ring. Theorem P(a) stands; checks (A)-(D) in e1checks.out all return 0.
escalations.repair: s08_connection_4 l.79: say the factor computation is done additively in B (as in the reason field), with T_z fixing the symbols and log q := -5 log 5L + sum_j log(L-zeta^j). Add one line: for an affine a with slope alpha, eps_a: W=1/Y -> z/a(L+t), log Y -> log a - log z, satisfies T_z o eps_a = eps_a o tau_alpha, where tau_alpha: W -> W/(1+alpha W), log Y -> log Y + log(1+alpha W). By lem:fsp-stirfe, tau_m G - G = sum_{i=1}^m (log Y + log(1+i/Y)), where G = log Gst(1+Y). Summing the six differences gives log[q prod(5sigma+kz)/((sigma+z)^5-1)] in A_L[[t,z]]; then exponentiate. l.61: write the phase as S_0 - S_0(L) and the amplitude as chi A_St/A_St(L,0). s08_connection_5 l.10: change Q[X][[u]] to Q[X^{+-1}]((s)); l.8: apply lem:fsp-const before lem:fsp-cov.

escalations.title: lem:fsp-res (iii): the exponential under the substitution X -> X + chi, used in prop:con-res
escalations.reason: The last sentence of lem:fsp-res (iii) is true, but the proof does not justify it. A ring homomorphism that agrees with the substitution on Laurent polynomials does not determine the image of E=e^{-f_0/zh}, because E is neither a Laurent polynomial nor u-adically small. The missing step is short and needs only E'=g'E with g=-f_0/zh, which follows termwise from the finite-sum coefficients of e^{-P_±/zh}. By induction E^{(j)}=Y_j(g',...,g^{(j)})E, where Y_j are the complete Bell polynomials. Substituting x_i->g^{(i)}, t->chi then gives T(E)=E exp(T(g)-g). Continuity and multiplicativity handle e^{-f_1/zh} and beta. The result is e^{-f(X+chi)/zh}beta(X+chi), read with the convention of (ii). The use in prop:con-res matches exactly: f=W_V, f_1=(V-1)/Y, chi=Y(X)-X, beta=a_Y, f(X+chi)=hatW, and a_Y(Y(X))Y'=hat a. That gives Res_Y=Res_X=hatV. Theorem P(b), the glue and Theorem C are unaffected. A Python check to u^4 agreed (sanity only).
escalations.repair: a_formalsp_5.tex l.98, replace the last sentence of the proof of (iii) by: "For E:=e^{-f_0/zh}, g:=-f_0/zh one has E'=g'E (the coefficients of e^{-P_±/zh} are finite sums). By induction E^{(j)}=Y_j(g',...,g^{(j)})E, Y_j the complete Bell polynomials, sum_j Y_j t^j/j!=exp(sum_{i>=1}x_i t^i/i!), as Y_{j+1}=x_1Y_j+DY_j with Dx_i=x_{i+1}. The substitution x_i->g^{(i)}, t->chi is a u-adically continuous ring homomorphism Q[x][[t]]->k[zh^{-1}][X^{±1}][[u]], so E(X+chi)=E exp(sum_{i>=1}g^{(i)}chi^i/i!)=e^{-f_0(X)/zh}e^{-(f_0(X+chi)-f_0(X))/zh}. The map is u-adically continuous and k((zh^{-1}))[[u]]-linear, so it sends e^{-f_1/zh} to e^{-f_1(X+chi)/zh}; by multiplicativity Omega(X+chi)=e^{-f_0(X)/zh}(e^{-(f(X+chi)-f_0(X))/zh}beta(X+chi)), i.e. e^{-f(X+chi)/zh}beta(X+chi) in the convention of (ii)." In the statement (l.94), say that this exponential is read with the convention of (ii) and that beta is as Q in (ii).

No pinned statement contains it: Teleman Thm (2) in (1.15) and GJR18 Thm 4.1 only give the existence of some R. It is a theorem, and it is pinnable: GJR18 Lemma 5.2 eq. (16) is literally prop:set-cyclicLR(iii), and Teleman v3 Props 7.7, 8.2(ii), 8.4 and 8.7(ii) give it in general. The (QRR) value fixes the constants, and the note proves the uniqueness it needs (lem:gau-wkb). escalations.title: Misprints and readings in the quoted topological-recursion identification (DNOPS/DOSS) used for thm:mod-tr
escalations.reason: I checked the printed pages of DNOPS v2 and DOSS v1. DNOPS (2-33) is false as printed for the model curve: off the diagonal its leading term has the wrong sign (B_00 against -B_00), and on the diagonal the delta term is missing. thm:mod-tr Step 1 (s06_model_3 l.23, l.28) rests this hypothesis only on DNOPS's claim that compact curves satisfy (2-33) and on the sentence before DNOPS Thm 8.1. Both are claims about this false identity, and the correct global statement (Eynard App. B, LPSZ) is not a declared input. So as written the step is unjustified, not just misprinted. The correct form (DOSS (4-1)) holds for the model curve: I give a three-step proof via d1(B/dx1)+d2(B/dx2) = sum_k dxi^k(x)dxi^k and lem:mod-laplace(i); checked exactly, and numerically to 1e-45 for all 15 pairs (i,j). The other five points are correctly minor: the index reading is DNOPS's own left-action convention, and the leg identity confirms it while the transpose fails. With these corrections, (Q) gives exactly what thm:mod-tr and prop:mod-Rtr use. A, B, C and Gamma are unaffected.

No PPZ proposition is used over N⊗Q(zeta), Q(zeta)[[q]] or Q[[u]]; there only definitions, (8) and lemmas proved in the note enter. The cohomology causes no issue: H*(Mbar,Q) is finite-dimensional and every operation is an A-linear extension. The cited reason, "polynomial in the coefficients", does not prove the claim, as X5 says. X5's fix of embedding into C is incomplete because PPZ is stated over Q. The claim is still true. PPZ's proofs are formal, including those of 2.3, 2.7, 2.9 and Lemma 2.11 used inside 2.12; L1-1 is confirmed as bookkeeping. Alternatively, every use takes a semisimple TFT and symplectic R = exp(r), which are freely parametrised. The conclusions are then polynomial identities that hold at all rational points, so they hold over every Q-algebra. The chain is unaffected.

escalations.title: What Corollary B states: representative-dependence, injectivity of ev, and frame change versus analytic continuation
escalations.reason: (a) ev is injective, so X4's m2 argument is correct. ev is injective exactly when L, l, C_0^(0..3) and I~_1^(0..2) are algebraically independent. The differential Galois group of PF4 is Sp_4 (Beukers-Heckman and Schlesinger). The pair (C_0, I_1) is isotropic and its stabiliser has dimension 3, so its jets have transcendence degree 7. log q is transcendental over the Picard-Vessiot field, because Sp_4 is perfect. The concomitant relation removes I~^(3). This is an undeclared external input, but nothing uses it. With it, F_g^N is the only preimage of F_g, so representative-dependence does not arise. (b) Theorems A, C, Gamma, Corollary B and rmk:int-constant claim exactly what is proved. The proof chain is unaffected. C_{alpha,beta} is a formal frame change, not analytic continuation: by irreducibility, the continuation of C_0 contains varpi_1 log u. Three sentences read as more than is proved: the abstract's "factorise the R-matrix", def:set-points l.28, and sec:sgn-lit l.106/108. In CGYZ's sense the last needs F_g^N in S, which l.108 calls "not needed". It holds by a checked few-line argument that uses Theorem C.

Add to What is not claimed: "Nothing is claimed about the analytic continuation of F_g to u=0; C_{alpha,beta} is a formal change of isotropic frame." sec:sgn-lit l.108: replace "is not needed" with the argument. F_g^N is l-free and a_k-invariant, so it lies in Q[L^{±1}][c_0^{±1},c_1,c_2,c_3,pi_1,pi_2][W^{-1}], with pi_j=i_j-i_0c_j/c_0. By D=1, sigma: L->zeta L permutes the colours, so its L-degrees are divisible by 5. Hence F_g^N lies in S and F_g^cf equals the CGYZ expansion of F_g. Alternatively restrict l.106 to "in the sense of Corollary B". Optionally add the injectivity remark to def:mai-Fcf l.81.

escalations.title: Formulas behind notational findings on the chain: eta^{-1} in the outer edge, Delta-hat in lem:flh-inputs, dilaton homogeneity for formal y, the hatted unit
escalations.reason: All five points are wording only; read literally, every chain formula is right and nothing misread is used. eta^{-1} in def:set-outer is the inverse bivector (def:set-graphsum, def:flh-outer(iii)); its lowered matrix is eta, and every matrix eta^{-1} (rmk:flh-fail(iii), cor:mai-gap, lem:flh-inputs(iii)) is the correct pairing. Misreading it rescales the edge by 1/25 (checked). The appendix hat-Delta (b_signs l.32) is cited nowhere; lem:flh-inputs(iv) uses def:set-modcohft. lem:set-dilaton(iii): for formal y each y-monomial gets one convergent series in b; lem:flh-dil substitutes y in z^2V[[z]]. lem:flh-hat: in hatted lowered coordinates (def:set-hat), hat-1 = s1 has components 5e_3 and q_hat = s^{-3}q(s^4 zh) (checked). Theorem A's TFT must be the conifold expansion (zeta^{4i}s varpi_0)^{2g-2+n}, the only reading that makes sense and the one the proof uses.
